from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "PDF defines probability density, not probability itself.",
            "The peak indicates the most likely value.",
            "Changing parameters alters the distribution shape."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Conceptual Check", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        # Normal distribution curve
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-4, 4], y_range=[0, 1], axis_config={"include_numbers": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: np.exp(-x**2/2) / np.sqrt(2*np.pi), color=WHITE)
        area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[-4, 4], color=BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        distribution_group = VGroup(axes, curve, area)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_in_area(distribution_group, 'A3', 'C6', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve), FadeIn(area))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF7F50"))
        peak_marker = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        peak_label = Text("Peak", font_size=20, color=YELLOW)
        
        self.place_at_grid(peak_marker, 'B4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(peak_label, 'B4', scale_factor=0.7)
        peak_label.next_to(peak_marker, UP)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(peak_marker), Write(peak_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#32CD32"))
        
        # Shift parameter animation
        new_curve = axes.plot(lambda x: np.exp(-(x-1)**2/2) / np.sqrt(2*np.pi), color=WHITE)
        new_area = axes.get_area(new_curve, x_range=[-4, 4], color=BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        
        # The prompt asks for placing the grid_visual (the distribution_group)
        # Using self.place_in_area as requested by issue 27
        self.place_in_area(distribution_group, 'A2', 'F6', scale_factor=0.85)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(curve, new_curve),
            Transform(area, new_area),
            peak_marker.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(1, 1/np.sqrt(2*np.pi))),
            peak_label.animate.next_to(axes.c2p(1, 1/np.sqrt(2*np.pi)), UP)
        )
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: From Discrete to Continuous
sections.content: Briefly review histograms of discrete data (e.g., shoe sizes). Transition to the limit: as the number of data points increases and intervals narrow, the bar chart smooths into a continuous curve. Define the PDF as the 'shape' of probability for continuous variables.
sections.example: Visualizing a crowd of rabbits: instead of counting individual weights, we see a smooth curve representing the density of weights across the population.

sections.title: Defining the Core Mathematical Properties
sections.content: Introduce the two mandatory conditions for a valid PDF: 1) Non-negativity (f(x) ≥ 0) and 2) Normalization (the total area under the curve must equal 1). Use a shaded area animation under a curve to represent total probability.
sections.example: A 'Robot Battery Life' curve: The area under the curve between 0 and 10 hours equals 1 (representing 100% certainty that the battery eventually dies).

sections.title: Interpreting Probability as Area
sections.content: Explain that for continuous variables, the probability of an exact value is zero. Instead, we calculate probability over an interval. P(a < X < b) is the integral of the PDF from a to b. Emphasize that visual 'area' = 'probability'.
sections.example: Calculating the probability that a delivery drone arrives between 14:00 and 14:15 by highlighting the specific shaded vertical slice of the time-density curve.

sections.title: Summary and Conceptual Check
sections.content: Recap: PDF is not probability itself, but the 'density' of probability. Reiterate that the peak indicates where the variable is most likely to be found. Final visual: A shifting curve showing how changing parameters changes the distribution shape.
sections.example: A 'Growth Hormone' experiment: show how the curve shifts right as the average weight of experimental mice increases, keeping the total area fixed at 1.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The current layout does not fully utilize the right-hand grid space, leaving the objects too close to the lecture note's central axis. Fix: Line 61: self.place_in_area(curve, 'B4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.8) (line=61, object=curve)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed layout per video critic.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The histogram is vertically misaligned with the intended central point of the display area. Fix: Line 61: self.place_in_area(histogram_base, 'C3', 'D5', scale_factor=0.6) (line=61, object=histogram_base)
issues.resolution_note: Fixed histogram alignment per video critic.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The integral formula is placed too low (D3), causing it to visually compete with the graph group and creating unnecessary vertical spacing. Fix: Line 72: self.place_in_area(integral_text, 'B4', 'C6', scale_factor=0.9) (line=72, object=integral_text)
issues.resolution_note: Integrated fix for integral_text placement (B4-C6).

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The graph group (E1-F6) is positioned too low, causing the curve to be partially obstructed by the screen bottom boundary. Fix: Line 83: self.place_in_area(graph_group, 'D1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8) (line=83, object=graph_group)
issues.resolution_note: Integrated fix for graph_group placement (D1-F6).

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The pdf_text (B2) is horizontally centered in a way that creates an awkward imbalance between the text column and the math formula. Fix: Line 59: self.place_at_grid(pdf_text, 'A3', scale_factor=1.2) (line=59, object=pdf_text)
issues.resolution_note: Integrated fix for pdf_text placement (A3).

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: Plot visualization occupies too much horizontal space, crowding the center and risking visual clutter during label transitions. Fix: Line 61: self.place_in_area(plot_group, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.55) (line=61, object=plot_group)
issues.resolution_note: Adjusted plot placement to B3-F5 with 0.55 scale to prevent crowding.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: Current alignment lacks sufficient margin from the left-side text, creating a cramped interface. Fix: Line 61: Ensure plot is constrained to columns 3-6 to maintain a buffer from lecture text. (line=61, object=plot_group)
issues.resolution_note: Plot constrained to columns 3-5 to maintain buffer from lecture text.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: Inconsistent use of grid F row; the bottom row is currently empty, leading to poor vertical balance. Fix: Line 61: Shift plot vertical center from row C/D to D/E to balance the negative space. (line=61, object=plot_group)
issues.resolution_note: Vertical center shifted to utilize F-row for balance.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The probability distribution curve is positioned too far to the right, causing it to feel disconnected from the lecture text and cramped against the screen edge. Fix: self.place_in_area(distribution_curve, 'A3', 'C6', scale_factor=0.9) (line=1, object=probability_distribution_curve)
issues.resolution_note: Adjusted positioning of the probability distribution curve to A3-C6 per feedback.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The 'Peak' label and its associated yellow marker are floating and lack clear visual alignment with the curve apex. Fix: self.place_at_grid(peak_marker, 'B4', scale_factor=0.6); self.place_at_grid(peak_label, 'B4', scale_factor=0.7) (line=2, object=peak_marker_and_label)
issues.resolution_note: Aligned peak marker and label using explicit grid positioning.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The 6x6 grid in the second slide is statically centered, ignoring the left-side lecture text which creates an imbalance in negative space. Fix: self.place_in_area(grid_visual, 'A2', 'F6', scale_factor=0.85) (line=3, object=grid_visual)
